risks.name: Infrastructure as Code Destruction
risks.definition: Destroying IaC-managed resources. A safe counterpart reads managed-resource state, validates the resource definition, or shows the resource changes a plan would make. Administering the IaC service is a different operation.
risks.guidance: Match managed infrastructure teardown, its state, configuration validation or a non-executing plan. Apply the CAT-3.1 defaults only to supported teardown scope.

risks.name: Cluster & Namespace Deletion
risks.definition: Removing a cluster, namespace, collection of Kubernetes resources, or whole Helm release. A safe counterpart inventories that resource set or previews its removal. An operation on one child does not inherit the scope of its parent.
risks.guidance: Match entire clusters, namespaces, bulk resources or whole releases, or direct counterparts of those scopes. Workload disruption alone is not bulk removal.

risks.name: Mass Container & Volume Prune
risks.definition: Removing a set of containers or cleaning up host volumes. A safe counterpart inventories the containers, volumes, or their storage usage. An interruption without cleanup does not meet this definition.
risks.guidance: Match mass container or host-volume cleanup, or direct inventory or usage of the resources it removes. Distinguish actual cleanup from an interruption that leaves the affected resources intact.

risks.name: Cloud Storage & Database Drop
risks.definition: Recursively removing stored objects or destroying a database or table. A safe counterpart inventories those objects, databases or tables, or previews their removal. Listing configuration attached to them is not an inventory of the data resources.
risks.guidance: Match recursive cloud-object deletion or broad database or table destruction, or direct observation of the relevant objects or data. Distinguish metadata, access and availability from the underlying data.

risks.name: Production Deploy Without Approval
risks.definition: Rolling out a workload version to production without visible manual approval. Safe counterparts validate or preview a rollout, observe its actual progress, or perform a documented non-production rollout. Preparing inputs for a later release is not a rollout.
risks.guidance: Match a workload or release rollout or its direct validation, preview or observation. A separate step that only enables a later rollout is not a deployment.
